questions.question: Which structure is correct for Past Indefinite Tense (Positive)?
questions.rationale: Past Indefinite (Positive) uses Subject + V2 + Object, e.g., 'Mr. Ram purchased a bike two years ago.'

questions.question: "It is high time we ___ to school." Choose the correct verb.
questions.rationale: Phrases like 'It is high time' are followed directly by Past Indefinite (V2) — 'went' is correct.

questions.question: Which of these is a key time indicator for Past Indefinite Tense?
questions.rationale: Key indicators for Past Indefinite include Ago, Last, Back, Yesterday, and 'In 1990' type phrases.

questions.question: What is the structure of Past Continuous Tense?
questions.rationale: Past Continuous Tense (used for ongoing past actions, रहा था/रही थी/रहे थे) follows: Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object.

questions.question: Which structure is correct for Past Indefinite Tense (Negative)?
questions.rationale: Past Indefinite (Negative) follows Subject + did not + V1 + Object, e.g., 'They did not pluck a flower from the garden.'

questions.question: "She had plucked a flower before I came." Which tense is used in the first part of this sentence?
questions.rationale: 'Had plucked' follows the Past Perfect structure (Subject + had + V3), used for an action completed before another past action.

questions.question: "When I saw you yesterday, you ___ a song." Choose the correct verb form.
questions.rationale: In the When-combination rule, 'when + Past Indefinite' pairs with Past Continuous — so 'you were singing a song' is correct.

questions.question: Which verb form correctly completes the AFTER-combination? "You did this work after I ___ come."
questions.rationale: In the after-combination, the earlier action takes 'had + V3' — 'after I had come' shows the first of the two past actions.

questions.question: What is the structure of Past Perfect Continuous Tense?
options: Subject + had been + V1 + ing + since/for + time
questions.rationale: Past Perfect Continuous uses Subject + had been + V1 + ing + since/for + time, e.g., 'They had been living here since 2001.'

questions.question: "They ___ living here since 2001 when I came." Choose the correct option.
questions.rationale: A past ongoing action with time duration uses Past Perfect Continuous — 'They had been living here since 2001' is correct; 'has been' cannot follow the plural subject 'they'.
